items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $ with decidable equality, the function $\operatorname{rootMultiplicity}(a, p) $ returns the largest natural number $ n $ such that the linear factor $ X - a $ divides the polynomial $ p $ exactly $ n $ times. If $ p $ is the zero polynomial, it returns $ 0 $. This is computed by finding the minimal $ n $ where $ (X - a)^{n+1} $ does not divide $ p $, leveraging the finite multiplicity property of linear factors in polynomial rings.

items.informal_name: Hilbert Polynomial Vanishes for Degrees Bounded by Root Multiplicity at One
items.type:

items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ over a field $ F $ and a natural number $ d $, if $ d \leq \text{rootMultiplicity}_1(p) $, then the Hilbert polynomial $ \text{HilbertPoly}(p, d) $ is zero. This means that when the degree parameter $ d $ does not exceed the multiplicity of the root $ 1 $ in $ p $, the corresponding Hilbert polynomial evaluation yields zero.
